title: Shallow Alignment Depth Across Model Families: A Comparative Replication

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: replicate shallow alignment finding across models, determine if it is universal or training-regime-dependent, directly informing which open-source models are safer to deploy. Every link is explicit and defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prefilling attacks are well-documented in Qi et al. and AISafetyLab toolkit. Uses publicly available models via HuggingFace. Beginners with a mentor can follow the replication methodology, though loading multiple large models on Colab Pro requires some care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a comparison table of alignment depth across model families. Single well-defined experiment with clear metric (refusal rate at token depth). Could be tight within 30 hours if limited to 3-4 models.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (2024) 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' (ICLR 2025 Outstanding Paper) already established the shallow alignment phenomenon. Follow-up work includes 'Why Is RLHF Alignment Shallow? A Gradient Analysis' (2026) and 'Matching Ranks Over Probability Yields Truly Deep Safety Alignment' which extends the analysis across models. The core contribution of this idea — comparing alignment depth across model families — is substantially covered by existing literature. The remaining gap is a systematic side-by-side replication table, but the methodology and findings are well-established.
